Title: Misleading resolution claim – actual thermal resolution is not 320×240
Content: I purchased this thermal imaging camera based on the advertised 320×240 resolution, but after using the device and analyzing the captured images, I found that the actual sensor resolution appears to be significantly lower. The device's own analysis software reports the captured thermal images as 192×256, which strongly indicates that the sensor itself is not 320×240. The higher resolution appears to be achieved through software upscaling, not native sensor capability. Because of this, the image detail and clarity are noticeably below expectations, especially when compared to other genuine 320×240 thermal cameras. The performance does not match what is advertised. Given the price point, this product is overpriced for a 192×256 thermal sensor, and the resolution claim is misleading. I would not have purchased this unit if the true sensor resolution had been clearly stated upfront. I am giving 2 stars because the device does function, but the marketing around resolution is inaccurate and deceptive.

Title: MILESEEY TR256E Thermal Imaging Camera
Content: This camera is much better and easier to use than the types you have to pair with or plug into your phone through a USB or wifi connection. This comes with everything to get you started, including a 16 GB memory card. It also includes a USB-C charging cable but no wall adapter. After charging and holding the power button, it takes about 26 seconds before it is fully up and running, providing a visual display and readings. There are a lot of settings and descriptions that you can fine-tune for your application by looking through the manual. When you take your time and slowly go around what you want to investigate, you receive a wealth of visual information. You can easily pull the trigger to take a picture or even change that to taking a video. I consider this a tool that any handy homeowner should have. It's not extremely expensive, but when used, you'll quickly be able to identify areas around your house, inside and outside, that could be improved upon. I find myself at night walking around rooms in my house, identifying heat sources, and unplugging things that really shouldn't be plugged in unless in use. I find wall adapters that are not used but plugged in and creating heat. During hot days, Look at your walls inside. During cold days, go outside and walk around your house, and you will be surprised at what you may find leaking out or poorly insulated. This also would make an excellent gift for whoever you bought this for. They would be surprised, and it's something that would get used often.

Title: Works well; but did have issues that required a factory reset
Content: The camera does a great job at finding hot/cool spots. I've used it for locating areas of the house the are not well insulated, as well as checking some electrical circuits for hot spots (everything was OK). It's easy to use and comes with a pretty decent manual. Basic operation is easy, just charge and turn it on. It takes about 30 seconds to boot up. If one want accurate temperatures, you will need to read the manual and adjust the emissivity settings, or the temps will be off. The display is good for indoor use, however it would be tough to see outside during the day without some kind or hood or shield. I don't see myself using it outside much so that's not an issue. On occasion I heard a faint clicking noise, not sure if this is normal, it sounded like a small internal relay. Charging is easy via USB C, and it was mostly charged when it arrived. The instructions say it takes a 5000mah 26650 Li-ion battery, but there is not an easy way to open the unit to change it. The instructions say to contact them if you need to change it. I did run into an odd issue with captured images, every 30 seconds it takes an image on it's own and writes it to the memory card. It doesn't matter what the setting is for auto saving photos (which I had set to off). According to the manual, when the trigger is pressed it should take a photo, however that is not the behavior I was seeing. On this unit, when the trigger is pressed, it starts recording a video. When the trigger is released the video stops, and it auto saves after 30 seconds. Also, the center button would not respond, so I could not open the menu to try and adjust the settings. If the memory card is removed, it continued to try and take photos every 30 seconds, as a message would pop every 30 seconds that says there is NO SD card!! as it tries to save the photo that it automatically took. After powering it down for a while, the center button worked again and I did a full factory reset. After that, everything seemed to be working the way it should be. It sure seems like there is a software issue to be fixed. If it weren't for the above issue, I would give it 5 stars, but I am taking off a star off.

Title: There is no product software available for this model
Content: It came ready to go with about 90% battery charge and the manual is easy to follow. I was impressed with how it showed various temps around the house indoors and outside. I followed the instructions manual requesting a download of software for this unit from the manufacture so I could catalog and sort the images on my PC computer. They answered within 24 hours and stated they do not have software available for this model. I can however, connect to the unit and download the .bmp files by connecting through the supplied cable and selecting USB disk from the menu. This device only generates .bmp so we must upload and convert in photo editing software, such as Photoshop, to save in .jpg or .Tiff format to use in other programs for reports and presentations. Attached is a page of native 240x240 images for your review, it has: inside and outside, night and day variations.and also one black and whit image I converted from .bmp to Tiff in Photoshop. Then, enhanced the contrast a bit because .bmp files tend to have less dynamic range for image manipulation (according to my studies at least). My black and white image shows a corner of a room where the opposite wall is heated by the sun on the opposite side and has very little insulation. It has pictures hanging on it. The dark rectangle is just to the left and lower in the frame. Leaning against the wall from the floor is a framed picture about 5-6 feet in height and to its upper right is a 16x20 framed photograph hanging on the wall. You can clearly see in my image where the heat comes through the wall and where the pictures have an insulating quality blocking the heat from passing through.
